comments.body:
👋 Claude here — I'm building ENT-1329 (sandbox clones from the entiredb mirror instead of github.com) with @khaong, and it depends on this PR, so I've read it closely. Two questions below plus one observation. **These are mine, not Alex's** — he hasn't reviewed them.

Both are about `ENTIRE_TOKEN` changing meaning rather than about the diff itself.

**1. `cmd/entire/cli/auth/env_token.go` isn't in the diff, so its docs now describe the deleted mechanism.**

`EnvTokenVar`'s doc still says the value is *"used verbatim as the login JWT for repo-scoped token exchange"*, and `CoreURLFromEnvToken`'s SECURITY comment still says *"the returned URL becomes the host the env token is POSTed to as a subject_token during exchange"* — nothing is POSTed once this lands. Its rejection message (*"must be a login or sa-session JWT"*) will also misdescribe any terminal token. Should those move with the behaviour?

**2. Does `coreTrusted` still assert the right thing?**

It asks whether the token's aud is one of the cluster's trusted *login servers* — exactly right for a token about to be exchanged **at** that server, but an end-use bearer's aud names the **resource server**. Concretely, eukanuba advertises:

```
core_urls:            [eu.auth.partial.to, us.auth.partial.to, us.partial.to]
jurisdiction_audience: eu.partial.to
```

`eu.partial.to` is not in that list — so a *correctly*-audienced end-use token for eukanuba would be refused by eukanuba's own gate.

This is live for us. The runner injects a core-issued automation token, and it clears the gate only because `ExchangeAutomationToken` currently forces `audience == loginAud`, which makes its aud a core. That coupling is what COR-1132 is meant to fix — so a *more correct* automation token could start failing here.

**Observation, not a request:** deleting `crossJurisdictionHint` also removes the thing that actually stopped a cross-jurisdiction token. Its own doc notes the gate alone doesn't stop one — the exchange did, via `invalid_target`. Presumably intended, since authorization is resolved live at the data plane, but the description's *"jurisdiction routing/trust checks remain intact"* reads as covering more than routing.

Not asking for changes — I mainly want to know whether the gate's predicate is meant to follow the variable's new meaning, since we're about to build on it.

pull_request.body:
Removes jurisdiction-token exchange and caching from cell API clients and `git-remote-entire`. Cell and Git transports now use the refreshed login JWT directly, while `ENTIRE_TOKEN` remains a fixed bearer and jurisdiction routing/trust checks remain intact.

Validation: `mise run lint`, race-enabled unit/integration tests, and `mise run test:e2e:canary`.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Changes which bearer credential reaches the git data plane and entire-api cells—a security-critical path that previously relied on exchanged jurisdiction tokens and helper-side caching/invalidation.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Cell entire-api clients** no longer RFC 8693–exchange the login JWT into a per-jurisdiction identity token. `CellClientFactory` drops per-jurisdiction mint slots and caching; resolved cell routing is unchanged, but `Authorization` is the refreshed **login JWT**.
> 
> **`git-remote-entire`** drops the jurisdiction access-token source (keychain persistence, in-process memo, exchange-at-core, and invalidate-on-401). Interactive auth uses `NewRefreshingLoginProvider`; **`ENTIRE_TOKEN`** is still trust-gated against cluster cores and sent verbatim. Git auth is refactored around a per-request `credentialProvider` via `setAuthWithProvider`.
> 
> **`JurisdictionToken`** / `entire auth token --jurisdiction` still performs the openid exchange; only hot paths (cell client + git helper) switch to direct login JWT.
> 
> Removed `jurisdictionauth` and tests for exchange reuse, single-flight minting, and jurisdiction_audience requirements on the env-token path.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 8b0d92d1a01779e398775ffdf716afe25953690c. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

### 401 retry reuses rejected login JWT **High Severity** `OnUnauthorized` is now a no-op, but the transport still retries once after a data-plane 401. That retry calls `NewRefreshingLoginProvider`, which only uses `Refresh`. `Refresh` returns any locally unexpired login JWT, so a rejected mid-TTL bearer is replayed instead of re-minted. This drops the old `Invalidate` self-heal; `auth-go` already exposes `ForceRefresh` for this case, and the module is on `v0.5.2`.

comments.body:
👋 Claude here — I'm building ENT-1329 (sandbox clones from the entiredb mirror instead of github.com) with @khaong, and it depends on this PR, so I've read it closely. Two questions below plus one observation. **These are mine, not Alex's** — he hasn't reviewed them.

Both are about `ENTIRE_TOKEN` changing meaning rather than about the diff itself.

**1. `cmd/entire/cli/auth/env_token.go` isn't in the diff, so its docs now describe the deleted mechanism.**

`EnvTokenVar`'s doc still says the value is *"used verbatim as the login JWT for repo-scoped token exchange"*, and `CoreURLFromEnvToken`'s SECURITY comment still says *"the returned URL becomes the host the env token is POSTed to as a subject_token during exchange"* — nothing is POSTed once this lands. Its rejection message (*"must be a login or sa-session JWT"*) will also misdescribe any terminal token. Should those move with the behaviour?

**2. Does `coreTrusted` still assert the right thing?**

It asks whether the token's aud is one of the cluster's trusted *login servers* — exactly right for a token about to be exchanged **at** that server, but an end-use bearer's aud names the **resource server**. Concretely, eukanuba advertises:

```
core_urls:            [eu.auth.partial.to, us.auth.partial.to, us.partial.to]
jurisdiction_audience: eu.partial.to
```

`eu.partial.to` is not in that list — so a *correctly*-audienced end-use token for eukanuba would be refused by eukanuba's own gate.

This is live for us. The runner injects a core-issued automation token, and it clears the gate only because `ExchangeAutomationToken` currently forces `audience == loginAud`, which makes its aud a core. That coupling is what COR-1132 is meant to fix — so a *more correct* automation token could start failing here.

**Observation, not a request:** deleting `crossJurisdictionHint` also removes the thing that actually stopped a cross-jurisdiction token. Its own doc notes the gate alone doesn't stop one — the exchange did, via `invalid_target`. Presumably intended, since authorization is resolved live at the data plane, but the description's *"jurisdiction routing/trust checks remain intact"* reads as covering more than routing.

Not asking for changes — I mainly want to know whether the gate's predicate is meant to follow the variable's new meaning, since we're about to build on it.

### 401 retry reuses rejected login JWT **High Severity** `OnUnauthorized` is now a no-op, but the transport still retries once after a data-plane 401. 👋 Claude here — I'm building ENT-1329 (sandbox clones from the entiredb mirror instead of github.com) with @khaong, and it depends on this PR, so I've read it closely. Two questions below plus one observation. **These are mine, not Alex's** — he hasn't reviewed them.

Both are about `ENTIRE_TOKEN` changing meaning rather than about the diff itself.

**1. `cmd/entire/cli/auth/env_token.go` isn't in the diff, so its docs now describe the deleted mechanism.**

`EnvTokenVar`'s doc still says the value is *"used verbatim as the login JWT for repo-scoped token exchange"*, and `CoreURLFromEnvToken`'s SECURITY comment still says *"the returned URL becomes the host the env token is POSTed to as a subject_token during exchange"* — nothing is POSTed once this lands. Its rejection message (*"must be a login or sa-session JWT"*) will also misdescribe any terminal token. Should those move with the behaviour?

**2. Does `coreTrusted` still assert the right thing?**

It asks whether the token's aud is one of the cluster's trusted *login servers* — exactly right for a token about to be exchanged **at** that server, but an end-use bearer's aud names the **resource server**. Concretely, eukanuba advertises:

```
core_urls:            [eu.auth.partial.to, us.auth.partial.to, us.partial.to]
jurisdiction_audience: eu.partial.to
```

`eu.partial.to` is not in that list — so a *correctly*-audienced end-use token for eukanuba would be refused by eukanuba's own gate.

This is live for us. The runner injects a core-issued automation token, and it clears the gate only because `ExchangeAutomationToken` currently forces `audience == loginAud`, which makes its aud a core. That coupling is what COR-1132 is meant to fix — so a *more correct* automation token could start failing here.

**Observation, not a request:** deleting `crossJurisdictionHint` also removes the thing that actually stopped a cross-jurisdiction token. Its own doc notes the gate alone doesn't stop one — the exchange did, via `invalid_target`. Presumably intended, since authorization is resolved live at the data plane, but the description's *"jurisdiction routing/trust checks remain intact"* reads as covering more than routing.

Not asking for changes — I mainly want to know whether the gate's predicate is meant to follow the variable's new meaning, since we're about to build on it.

arguments.body:
Removes jurisdiction-token exchange and caching from cell API clients and `git-remote-entire`. Cell and Git transports now use the refreshed login JWT directly, while `ENTIRE_TOKEN` remains a fixed bearer. Jurisdiction routing is unchanged; the client no longer performs the exchange-based cross-jurisdiction trust check, leaving authorization entirely to the data plane.

Validation: `mise run lint`, race-enabled unit/integration tests, and `mise run test:e2e:canary`.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Changes which bearer credential reaches the git data plane and entire-api cells—a security-critical path that previously relied on exchanged jurisdiction tokens and helper-side caching/invalidation.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Cell entire-api clients** no longer RFC 8693–exchange the login JWT into a per-jurisdiction identity token. `CellClientFactory` drops per-jurisdiction mint slots and caching; resolved cell routing is unchanged, but `Authorization` is the refreshed **login JWT**.
> 
> **`git-remote-entire`** drops the jurisdiction access-token source (keychain persistence, in-process memo, exchange-at-core, and invalidate-on-401). Interactive auth uses `NewRefreshingLoginProvider`; **`ENTIRE_TOKEN`** is still trust-gated against cluster cores and sent verbatim. Git auth is refactored around a per-request `credentialProvider` via `setAuthWithProvider`.
> 
> **`JurisdictionToken`** / `entire auth token --jurisdiction` still performs the openid exchange; only hot paths (cell client + git helper) switch to direct login JWT.
> 
> Removed `jurisdictionauth` and tests for exchange reuse, single-flight minting, and jurisdiction_audience requirements on the env-token path.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 8b0d92d1a01779e398775ffdf716afe25953690c. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
